chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Imran ibn Ismail ibn Imran al-Qummi, who said:

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) the third [Imam], 'I have male and female children; is it permissible for me to give them something from the Zakat?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'That is permissible for you.'

key_terms.أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الثَّالِث: Abu al-Hasan the third (Imam Ali al-Rida, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: Can I give my Zakat money to my own children?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies a specific legal nuance in Shia jurisprudence: while parents are generally obligated to support their children from their own wealth (preventing them from being 'debtors' to the parent), they may still give Zakat to them if the children are eligible recipients (e.g., poor or in debt). Imam al-Hasan al-Askari (AS) confirms this permissibility, highlighting that the prohibition of giving Zakat to one's direct dependents applies primarily when the giver is financially responsible for their maintenance, but does not apply if the children qualify under the broader categories of Zakat recipients.
